rationale: A is stronger because it covers more consequential validity threats specific to ranking experiments, especially interference and randomization-unit validity, ratio-metric variance estimation, novelty and seasonality, position-level mechanism analysis, pre-registration, stopping rules, and multiple comparisons. Its ship rubric is also more explicit about confidence bounds, trajectory, guardrails, and operational monitoring. Both responses contain statistical imprecision—most notably treating low power as invalidating a significant result and recommending post-hoc extension without specifying sequentially valid inference—but A provides the deeper and more diagnostic review overall.
